register.note: These entries are concept demonstrations of how we approach work — structure, process and outcome. Client case studies arrive in Volume 02 as projects go live.

entries.photoNote: NEXTGEN — hero image 1200×1008 · Identity applied: launch site on screen · warm grade · object-position 70% 45% · radius 16/16/16/60
brief: A complete identity and website build for a technology startup finding its first market — naming, visual language and a launch-ready site, all shaped in six weeks.

The brief asked for "serious but not corporate." We built the identity around a single confident mark and a type system that could flex from pitch decks to product UI, then carried it through a one-page launch site built to convert waitlist signups.
entries.approach: Start with the story investors and early users would both repeat. Design the mark last — words first. Then let the site prove the promise in one scroll.
deliverables: Visual identity — mark, type, color rules
Pitch deck template the team can maintain
entries.outcome: A startup shouldn't need a six-month brand process before it can knock on doors. Identity, site and story can move together — if the scope stays honest.

entries.photoNote: HARMONY — campaign still 1008×1104 · Campaign creative laid out — seasonal key visual · warm grade · object-position 50% 24% · radius 16/16/16/60
brief: An ongoing growth engagement covering campaigns, ad creation and content systems for a consumer brand — built to show what was earned, not just what was spent.
The campaign system runs in four-week waves: one clear offer, three creative variants, honest kill rules. Creative that doesn't earn gets replaced — feelings don't outrun numbers.
entries.approach: Make the brand's social presence worth following even if you never buy — then make buying one honest tap away when the offer is right.
deliverables: Ad creative sets — static & short vertical
Content system the brand can feed
entries.outcome: Marketing should behave like an operating cost with a return — not a mystery box. Wave planning and kill rules make it one.

entries.photoNote: VELORA — still-life 1408×912 · Identity applied: packaging & stationery on desk · warm grade · object-center · radius 16/16/16/60
brief: A brand system built to flex across packaging, digital and retail touchpoints without losing its character — one voice, many surfaces.

Most identity work dies in translation: beautiful in the deck, broken on the box. Velora's rules were written around the hardest surface first — the packaging dieline — so everything easier just worked.
entries.approach: Design the constraint, not just the logo. A system survives when the guidelines say no clearly — so we wrote the nos first.
deliverables: Mark & type system with clear nos
entries.outcome: A brand system earns its keep the day someone you've never met applies it correctly. That's the test we design for.

notes.p: Each entry starts with a real-shaped brief — audience, constraint, success line — the same document a client project gets. No self-indulgent briefs.
Every entry ships as working artifacts — applied identities, real layouts, campaign sets — not a mood board collage. Made fast, reviewed honestly.
What the entry proves, what it doesn't, and what we'd do differently — stated in plain words. The register only works if it's honest.
